amal: FYI telemetry spotted wrapped KMS ciphertexts in partner-ingest logs that look like a local keystore leak. Seen across 3 consecutive ingest jobs, low volume but sensitive. tagging sec triage.

amal: ```
2025-07-12T11:02:13Z INFO ingest/handler.go: got blob id=blk-c2a1 wrap_ciphertext=CpY...
2025-07-12T11:02:16Z INFO ingest/handler.go: got blob id=blk-c2a2 wrap_ciphertext=CpY...
```

jonah: Ugh. Likely the container mounted a hostPath with keystore files during partner onboarding. Which KMS key was used?

linh: Looks like projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/keystore-wrap-v2 (primary v2). partner SA partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com had encrypter role granted for onboarding.

security-bot: ALERT: IAM activity — partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com called cloudkms.*encrypt* on keystore-wrap-v2 at 2025-07-12T11:03:01Z.

maria: Immediate actions I propose:
  - revoke encrypter privileges from partner SA NOW (linh)
  - create a fresh wrap key (keystore-wrap-v4) and enable dual-wrap support in ingest for 24h (jonah)
  - schedule a staged bulk rewrap (small batches, verify checksums)
  - rotate any long-lived customer tokens + CI runners that accessed those blobs
  - block hostPath / keystore mounts in ingest via admission controller and Terraform guardrails
  - increase Vault audit retention + add an alert for high wrap rate per SA

jonah: For dual-wrap I'll change the ingest writer to attempt dst-key encrypt first, then fallback to src-key decrypt->rewrap on read until rewrap cutover completes. I'll owner the rewrap script and do dry-run in staging. Example rewrap run (dry-run):

jonah: ```bash
# grant rewrap-runner encrypt rights on new key
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding \
  --key=keystore-wrap-v4 \
  --member=serviceAccount:rewrap-runner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
python infra/rewrap.py \
  --src projects/redwood-prod/.../keystore-wrap-v2 \
  --dst projects/redwood-prod/.../keystore-wrap-v4 \
  --blobs-file=gs://redwood-sec-exports/ephemeral-keystore-hitlist.json \
  --batch 100 --dry-run
```

linh: Revoking partner SA encrypt grants now. Also adding a Terraform RBAC patch to remove encrypter for that SA and only allow decrypt where strictly needed. Snippet I will push: 

linh: ```hcl
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "partner_remove_encrypt" {
  crypto_key_id = var.ingest_key
  role = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member = "serviceAccount:partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  # plan to replace with a custom role without encrypt in next PR
}
```

maria: Also add a Gate in CI: prevent workloads in the ingest namespace from setting hostPath mounts or mounting /var/keystore. We'll enforce via OPA/Gatekeeper. ops-bot can we add the constraint?

ops-bot: Creating constraint: gatekeeper constraint template + deny hostPath mounts under namespaces matching "ingest-*". PR: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/policies/pull/467

sre-oncall: I'll coordinate a 30m ingest deploy freeze to run the staging dry-run then a small prod batch. ETA 50m. I'll monitor decryption errors and roll back if >0.1% failure.

amal: Vault changes: set audit retention for ingest namespace to 90 days and add alert: wrap_calls_by_sa > 3/min => page. Also enable more verbose audit fields for KMS wrap operations.

linh: Adding transient alert rule and updating Vault config. Will attach PR link in 15m.

maria: Post-ops steps: rotate partner long-lived app tokens, CI runner keys that accessed the blobs, and any k8s Secrets referencing those ciphertexts. Add runbook item to revoke old wrap key versions after 72h with a final verification sweep.

jonah: Rewrap plan: 1) generate hitlist of affected blobs (who accessed them + checksums) -> export to controlled GCS 2) run dry-run rewrap in staging 3) run prod rewrap in small batches, validate consumer decrypts 4) flip ingest to prefer new key then retire old key versions after 72h. I'll capture metrics and hash comparisons per batch.

security-bot: Ticket opened: SEC-2181 "keystore hostPath exposure -> rewrap + RBAC + admission policy". Assignees: jonah, linh, maria, amal. Severity: P1.

amal: Good. After the bulk rewrap, please paste a short checklist (rewrap summary, rotated secrets list, admission control PR link, Vault audit PR). We'll run a short postmortem in 24-48h to update onboarding docs (no hostPath, use KMS or Vault providers) and add an automated test to detect wrapped ciphertexts in logs.

jonah: Will do. Starting staging dry-run now. I'll update thread with the dry-run summary and prod batch times.
